Industrial B2B producer with very little consumer awareness, although it has become part of the U.S. Steel brand.

China Media Capital, a Shanghai-based, state-backed private equity firm focused on media, entertainment and consumer technology. It was set up in 2009 by media executive Li Ruigang, with backing from state-owned groups and investors, and has invested in the Shanghai Disney resort partnership, film and TV businesses and sports and online video platforms. Revenue comes from investment returns and management fees on its funds. It is an investor rather than an operating consumer brand, so the profile is among Chinese media and finance executives, not the general public.

American coffee company that popularised the single-serve K-Cup pod system, making Keurig brewing machines and selling pods for dozens of brands, including its own Green Mountain Coffee Roasters, Tully's and Newman's Own Organics, as well as licensed Dunkin' and Starbucks pods. Customers are households and offices, and money comes from machine sales and recurring pod purchases. It was acquired by JAB Holding in 2016 for about 13.9 billion dollars and in 2018 merged with Dr Pepper Snapple to form Keurig Dr Pepper. Strong consumer brand across North America.

Chinese online healthcare company operating the Ping An Good Doctor platform, part of the Ping An insurance group, which provides online consultations with in-house doctors, family doctor services, health management, pharmacy delivery and hospital appointments to tens of millions of users. Revenue comes from health services, medical e-commerce and subscriptions, and some from insurers and enterprises. The Hong Kong-listed Ping An Healthcare and Technology (1833.HK) is its public entity, after fundraising from large investors. Strong consumer brand in China tied to the Ping An name, which also sponsors sport.

US healthcare technology company in Minneapolis providing a network that links providers and health plans for claims, eligibility checks, denial management and Medicare compliance, serving thousands of hospitals and many thousands of pharmacies and clinics. Revenue comes from software subscription and transaction fees. It was backed by Veritas Capital and Vista-linked investors and was acquired by Inovalon in 2021 for roughly 1.2 billion dollars. B2B healthcare IT with essentially no consumer awareness.

Indian telecom tower company that owned and operated about 35,000 mobile towers across India, leasing space to carriers like Airtel, Vodafone Idea and Reliance Jio. It was formed in 2007 and was majority owned by Bharti Airtel, listed on the NSE and BSE in 2012. In November 2020 Bharti Infratel merged with Indus Towers, forming a combined tower company with over 180,000 towers that took the Indus Towers name. B2B infrastructure with little public brand awareness.

The UK Catapult network, a group of not-for-profit technology and innovation centres set up and funded by Innovate UK to help businesses take new ideas to market, with each centre focused on an area such as satellite applications, offshore wind, cell therapy, digital, energy systems and transport. Customers are British companies, universities and research bodies, and income is a mix of government core funding, collaborative research and commercial contracts. Public-sector innovation bodies without consumer products, so minimal brand awareness beyond industry, and it is not a typical sponsor target.

Canadian gold miner that operated the Detour Lake open pit mine in northern Ontario, one of the largest gold mines in Canada, producing roughly 600,000 ounces a year at its peak. It sold its gold on world markets to refiners and bullion buyers. It was listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange and was acquired by Kirkland Lake Gold in January 2020, which later became part of Agnico Eagle. B2B commodity producer with little consumer profile.

Canada's export credit agency, a Crown corporation owned by the Government of Canada and operating on commercial principles, which provides insurance, loans, guarantees and equity to help Canadian companies export and invest abroad. Customers are Canadian exporters and their foreign buyers, from small firms to large corporations, and it earns interest and premiums. It operates from Ottawa with offices worldwide and supports tens of billions of dollars in trade each year. Public body with strong visibility among exporters and trade policymakers, but no consumer brand.

Chinese private health check-up provider operating medical examination centres in major cities, offering physical examinations, screening and health management services to corporate employees and individuals. Revenue comes from check-up packages sold to companies and consumers. It is sometimes called Health 100 or Jiankang 100, and it attracted large investment around 2019. Scale and ownership are not clear from the information available beyond that. Recognised in medical check-up circles in China, with a modest consumer profile.

US energy and mineral technology platform, shown in Crunchbase as applying technologies to energy and mining, and located in Austin, Texas. Funding was recorded in 2016. The description is cut off in the data, and the specific operations, assets, customers and ownership cannot be confirmed from the information available. There are several energy companies with similar names, so the identity is uncertain. Details should be verified on the website before outreach. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

South Korean financial group built around Mirae Asset Securities, one of Asia's leading brokerages, plus asset management, insurance and venture capital arms. Its global asset management division includes Global X ETFs in the US and Mirae Asset Global Investments, which together manage hundreds of billions of dollars. Customers are retail and institutional investors worldwide, and revenue comes from fees, trading commissions and investments. Founded in 1997 by Park Hyeon-joo, it is privately controlled with listed subsidiaries. Well-known financial brand in Korea with sports and cultural sponsorships.

Canadian gold mining company that owned the Brucejack mine in northern British Columbia, a high-grade underground gold mine that started production in 2017. It sold gold doré to refiners and later also produced concentrate. The shares traded in Toronto and New York. It was acquired by Newcrest Mining in 2022, and Newcrest was in turn bought by Newmont in 2023. B2B resource business with no consumer profile.

North American outpatient diagnostic imaging company providing MRI, CT, PET and other scans through a network of around 200 imaging centres, working with hospitals and radiology groups, with centres in the US. It was founded in Canada and listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange, then expanded by acquiring Alliance HealthCare Services in 2021 from a Stonepeak-backed deal. Heavy debt led to bankruptcy filing in 2023. Customers are patients, referring physicians and health plans. Healthcare provider with low national brand visibility.

US telehealth company that provides a platform for virtual visits between patients and doctors, supplying software and services to health systems, health plans and employers, and offering its own clinicians through the Amwell Medical Group. Revenue comes from subscriptions, visit fees and licences to large clients such as health plans, the US Department of Defense and hospitals. Founded in 2006 as American Well, it listed on the NYSE (AMWL) in 2020. Mostly B2B2C, so consumers see the Amwell name through partner apps, with moderate public awareness.

One of the world's biggest gold mining companies, with mines in Africa, Australia and the Americas, and a corporate base that moved from Johannesburg to London and a listing on the NYSE in 2023. It produces roughly 2.5 to 3 million ounces of gold a year, selling mainly to bullion refiners. Operations include Obuasi in Ghana, Kibali in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Sukari mine in Egypt. Heavily B2B with commodity sales, so little consumer awareness, although it is a major mining brand globally.

Beijing-based Chinese company in health care and information technology, shown as a technology company offering services in the medical field. Funding was recorded in 2021. The input does not include enough detail to say which products or platforms it provides, who its customers are or who owns it. It is probably a B2B health tech supplier with minimal consumer awareness. Details should be verified on the company website before outreach. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

US health benefits administrator that runs self-insured health plans for employers as a third party administrator, using technology to bring together claims, navigation, support and cost management in one platform. Customers are mid-sized and large employers like Lyft, Adobe and Red Bull, who cover tens of thousands to millions of employees. Revenue comes from per-member administration fees. Founded in 2013 and venture-funded by firms including GV, Founders Fund and Silver Lake. B2B employer health benefits business, with limited public consumer awareness.

Spanish media and sports rights company based in Barcelona, founded in 2000 by Jaume Roures, which produces and distributes TV content and films and holds major sports media rights, including La Liga international rights and the Spanish women's and men's competitions. It owns production arms such as Imagina and Mediapro Studio, and has invested in Chinese ownership via Orient Hontai Capital and Tencent. Customers include broadcasters, leagues and platforms worldwide. B2B media group with strong industry profile, and well known in football broadcasting.

Chinese online medical platform that connects patients with doctors for consultations, runs an online pharmacy and provides digital tools for physicians, based in Chengdu. It claims to have a very large number of registered doctors and tens of millions of users. Revenue comes from medical consultation fees, drugs and services, and from pharmaceutical marketing. Backed by firms such as Tencent. Moderate consumer awareness in China, mostly through health app downloads.

Chinese medical robotics company, a unit of MicroPort Scientific, developing the Toumai surgical robot system and orthopaedic and endovascular robots. Customers are hospitals in China and, increasingly, overseas, and revenue comes from robot sales, instruments and procedure consumables. Its Toumai system won approvals in China and entered international markets. The company listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange in 2021 (stock code 2252). Known among surgeons and hospital buyers, with limited consumer profile.

Beijing-based Chinese enterprise artificial intelligence and big data analytics company, also known as MiningLamp Technology, offering data intelligence tools and marketing and sales analytics to large clients such as consumer brands, automakers and telecoms. It was founded in 2014 by Wu Ming Hui and the chairman and raised capital from major investors, including Tencent. It listed in Hong Kong in 2023. B2B software with a profile among Chinese enterprise technology buyers, but little public consumer awareness.

New York-based digital pharmacy that delivers prescription medicines to customers' homes within hours, working with doctors, health systems and insurers, with its own mobile app and a network of local pharmacies in several US cities. Revenue comes from dispensing prescriptions and insurer reimbursements. It was founded in 2016 by Eric Kinariwala and raised capital from venture investors, reaching a multi-billion dollar valuation in 2021. Reasonable consumer awareness in the cities it serves, with a strong design-led brand.

US wound care company that manages hospital-based wound care centres, treating chronic wounds such as diabetic foot ulcers and pressure ulcers with hyperbaric oxygen therapy. It partners with more than 600 hospitals across the US and earns fees from them for running the programmes. Owned by private equity firms including Clearlake and Thomas H. Lee, and it came out of a 2023 restructuring. Healthcare operator with essentially no consumer brand awareness.

US home care technology company that provides in-home support for older adults through a network of caregivers matched to clients via an app. It acquired Home Instead in 2021, the franchise network with hundreds of franchises worldwide. Customers are seniors and their families. Revenue comes from hourly care fees paid privately or through insurers, with funding from investors including Thrive Capital and Tiger Global. Consumer awareness is modest and regional, but Home Instead has broader brand recognition in senior care.

Japan's long-established technology group, a supplier of IT services, network equipment, satellite systems, biometrics (including face recognition) and defence electronics. Customers are governments, telecom carriers, utilities and enterprises worldwide. NEC is more than a century old, employs over a hundred thousand people and is listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange. Known for NEC brand PCs historically and for global sports and event sponsorship, so it has decent consumer recognition in Japan and some markets worldwide.

Canadian lithium company that developed the Whabouchi spodumene mine in northern Quebec and a lithium hydroxide plant at Becancour. It aimed to sell battery-grade lithium chemicals to electric vehicle battery makers. The company went through creditor protection in 2019 and was restructured with support from Investissement Quebec. Customers would be battery cathode makers in North America and Asia. B2B resource and chemical company with no consumer awareness.

Premium international schools group running schools in dozens of countries, with students ranging from early years to sixth form across the Nord Anglia, British International, and Collège Alpin brands. Revenue comes from tuition fees paid by wealthy local and expatriate families, with schools across Asia, Europe, North America and the Middle East. It is owned by an investor consortium that includes Baring Private Equity Asia, CPPIB and Neuberger Berman after a 2017 take-private. It has partnerships with Juilliard, MIT and others. Strong reputation among international families.

South Korean mobility and navigation company, built around the T map navigation app, which provides turn-by-turn directions, parking, public transport and EV charging services to millions of drivers. It was formed from a SK Telecom unit and gained investment from Uber and Macquarie, forming a ride-hailing joint venture called UT. Revenue comes from advertising, subscription services, mobility fees and data. Dominant domestic navigation brand with a very high consumer awareness in South Korea.

English Premier League football club based in north London, playing at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, a 62,000-seat venue that also hosts NFL games and concerts. Revenue comes from broadcasting, matchday, commercial sponsorship (partners include AIA, Nike and Kia) and stadium events. The club is controlled by ENIC Group, led by Daniel Levy, and has a global fan base of hundreds of millions of followers. One of the best known football brands worldwide, with a very strong sponsorship platform.

Chinese insurtech and health crowdfunding platform whose core product is Shuidi Chou, a medical crowdfunding service, plus Shuidi Baoxian, an insurance marketplace selling health and critical illness policies, and a mutual aid product. Revenue comes mostly from insurance commissions. Founded in 2016, it listed on the NYSE in 2021 (ticker WDH). Users number in the hundreds of millions, so consumer awareness in China is high, although regulation of the sector has limited growth.

Canadian tri-government agency, funded by the federal, Ontario and City of Toronto governments, in charge of redeveloping Toronto's waterfront, including projects such as Quayside, the East Bayfront, Port Lands flood protection and the Don River re-naturalisation. It serves as a not-for-profit master developer, working with private developers and builders, and earns revenue from land sales and government funding. Famous for the Sidewalk Labs smart city proposal that was cancelled in 2020. Strong local profile in Toronto, but not a commercial brand.

US multi-state cannabis operator, selling cannabis flower, vapes, edibles and concentrates through its own retail dispensaries and wholesale channels in states such as Florida, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Massachusetts and New Jersey. The company is Miami-headquartered but trades on the Canadian Securities Exchange (AYR.A) and has dozens of dispensaries. Customers are medical and adult-use cannabis consumers. Cannabis is federally illegal in the US, which restricts advertising and sponsorship options, and the company has been under financial pressure.

US bitcoin mining company that uses its own mining rigs and sells its own computing power, based in Cincinnati, Ohio, and positioned itself as vertically integrated by designing and operating its own data centre infrastructure. It planned to go public through a SPAC merger with Adit EdTech, which eventually closed in 2023. Revenue comes from bitcoin mined and sold. B2B crypto infrastructure with little public awareness and volatile finances.

US healthcare data and analytics company that maintains a large map of patient journeys from billions of insurance claims, used by life sciences and health organisations to find patients, analyse treatment patterns and launch drugs. Customers include pharmaceutical firms, payers and providers, and revenue comes from software subscription plans such as its Healthcare Map platform. Founded in 2014 by Arif Nathoo and Web Sun, and backed by investors including Tiger Global and Andreessen Horowitz, with valuation above three billion dollars. B2B data business with little consumer awareness.

Norwegian oil and gas exploration company based in Stavanger that focuses on exploration licences on the Norwegian continental shelf. Business is to find and develop North Sea hydrocarbon prospects, often alongside bigger operators, and earn revenue from selling oil and gas once fields come online or by selling licence stakes. Details on its current ownership, licence portfolio and production are not well known to me, and the company's size is not clear from the available information. B2B energy business with no consumer brand profile.

Chinese online steel trading platform supported by the Baowu Steel Group, the world's largest steelmaker, matching sellers and buyers of steel products, and offering transactions, logistics, warehousing and financing services. Customers are steel mills, traders and manufacturers, and revenue comes from trading fees and related services. It was founded in 2015 and has raised capital from investors including Tencent. Platform sits in Baoshan, Shanghai, and is a major industrial e-commerce site in China. B2B, so little consumer visibility.

Spanish company based in Sant Cugat del Valles, which the name and location suggest is linked to Fluidra, the pool and wellness equipment group listed in Spain. Fluidra makes pumps, filters, cleaners, chemicals, heating and automation for residential and commercial pools, selling through installers and distributors under brands such as Zodiac, Astral, Jandy and Polaris. PRO appears to refer to the professional-oriented side of the business. The match is based on the HQ and the name only. Unclear scale, so details need checking. Sells to trade rather than consumers.

US company that offers air-to-ground wireless broadband for aircraft, a network of ground towers that provides high-speed internet to business jets, helicopters and commercial airlines, designed to deliver faster in-flight connectivity than conventional satellite or older air-to-ground systems. Customers are aircraft operators and avionics partners, and revenue comes from equipment installation and service subscriptions. The company raised several hundred million dollars from private investors over its life. B2B with low consumer awareness.

US value-based kidney care company that works with health plans and physician groups to manage patients with chronic kidney disease and keep them out of hospital and off dialysis for longer. It offers care teams, home visits and technology, and earns shared savings or per-patient fees from payers such as Medicare Advantage plans. It was founded in 2017 and backed by large investors including Tiger Global. B2B healthcare provider with little consumer brand awareness.

Peruvian agribusiness group that grows, packs and exports fresh fruit and vegetables, mainly avocados, blueberries, mandarins, grapes and asparagus, to supermarkets in North America, Europe and Asia. It owns thousands of hectares of farmland in Peru and elsewhere, and employs tens of thousands of people at peak harvest. Customers are retailers and food distributors, sold largely under customers' own brand labels. Controlled by Dyer family interests, and some of its shares have been listed on the London Alternative Investment Market. B2B supplier with little direct consumer awareness.

Luxembourg energy group that supplied electricity and natural gas, ran energy networks and offered mobility and energy services in Luxembourg, Germany and Belgium, previously known as Enovos International. The Luxembourg state, SNCI and other utilities held major stakes, and Creos operates the grid. In 2016 the group was rebranded Encevo as the parent, with the Enovos name remaining for retail energy supply. Customers are households, businesses and municipalities. Enovos is a recognised consumer energy brand in Luxembourg.

US long-term care and rehabilitation company that operated nursing homes, skilled nursing centres and assisted living, with rehab therapy services, across roughly 30 states, treating elderly and post-acute patients. Revenue came mainly from Medicare and Medicaid reimbursements. It was listed on the NYSE (GEN) and delisted in 2021 as financial pressure grew, and many of its facilities were sold or transferred to other operators. Healthcare provider with limited national brand recognition outside local communities.

DevSecOps platform sold as software that covers the whole software lifecycle in one application, from source code hosting and issue tracking to CI/CD pipelines, security scanning and deployment, offered as a SaaS product or self-managed. Customers are software teams at enterprises and startups, paying per-seat subscription tiers, with well over 30 million registered users and customers such as Goldman Sachs and Siemens. Founded by Sid Sijbrandij and Dmitriy Zaporozhets, it operates as a remote-first company and listed on Nasdaq (GTLB) in 2021. Strong brand among developers, but little consumer awareness.

Brazilian nickel development company that was advancing the Araguaia ferronickel project in Para and the Vermelho nickel-cobalt project, listed on the London AIM and the Toronto Stock Exchange. The plan was to sell nickel products to stainless steel and battery supply chains. It never reached full production, and after funding problems the company entered restructuring and administration proceedings in 2024. Before that it raised hundreds of millions of dollars from investors and lenders. B2B resource developer with no consumer profile, and not a realistic sponsor.

Australian commercial finance company that provides working capital to small and medium businesses, mainly through trade finance, invoice finance and payments services, also offering foreign exchange and other lending products. Customers are Australian SMEs that need cash while they wait for invoices to be paid, and revenue comes from fees and interest margins. It is listed on the Australian Securities Exchange and works through broker and accountant referrals. Small-cap financial brand with limited public awareness outside the business community.

US primary care provider for Medicare Advantage patients, running a network of more than 100 clinics across many states, mostly in underserved communities, and working under risk-based contracts where it is paid a set sum per patient to keep them healthy. Founded in Chicago in 2012 by Mike Pykosz, it listed on the NYSE (OSH) in 2020 and was acquired by CVS Health in 2023 for about 10.6 billion dollars. Customers are seniors and their insurers. Regional healthcare brand with a modest national consumer profile.

US software company offering AI-powered messaging, reviews, payments and lead conversion tools for local businesses such as car dealers, home services firms, medical practices and retailers, letting them text customers and collect payments and reviews. Revenue comes from monthly subscriptions, with tens of thousands of business customers. Founded in 2014 in Utah by Eric Rea and Dennis Steele and backed by Accel, GV and Summit Partners. B2B brand with significant name recognition among small business owners, though not the general public.

US medical aesthetics company that made breast implants, tissue expanders and body contouring products for plastic surgeons, with brands including Sientra textured implants, AlloX2 tissue expanders and the Vaser ultrasound platform. Customers were plastic surgeons and hospitals, and revenue came from device sales. It was listed on Nasdaq (SIEN) and went through a chapter 11 filing in 2024, with its assets bought by Tiger Aesthetics. B2B medical device maker, with a consumer brand presence mainly among breast surgery patients.

Mining company, based in Montreal, whose main asset was a majority stake in the huge Oyu Tolgoi copper and gold mine in Mongolia, one of the largest copper deposits in the world. Rio Tinto owned most of the shares and ran the mine, while the Mongolian government held a minority stake in the mine. Rio Tinto bought out the remaining minority shareholders in 2022, and the company stopped trading. Customers are metal smelters and traders, so it is a B2B commodity producer with no consumer brand.

Albuquerque-based technology company described as an IT solutions provider. The Crunchbase information is limited to a general summary of IT services, and the exact services, clients, size, and ownership cannot be confirmed from what is available. There is a possibility that this refers to a small federal or defence IT contractor, but that cannot be established. It is likely a B2B business with little consumer visibility. Details should be verified on its website before any approach. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Los Angeles-based investment management and asset management company, as described in the Crunchbase summary, tagged for asset management and finance. The data does not show its funds, strategy, client base, size or ownership, and there are other firms with similar names, so the identity is uncertain. It is probably an institutional or private investment business with no consumer brand. Details should be verified before outreach. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Italian biofuel and biochemical company formed as a joint venture between Mossi and Ghisolfi and the US private equity firm TPG, which built the Crescentino plant in Piedmont, the first commercial-scale cellulosic ethanol facility using straw and energy crops, with its PROESA process. Customers were fuel blenders and chemical companies. Financial problems and debt hit the venture, and it went into insolvency proceedings in 2017. Industrial B2B technology business with no consumer brand profile, and now essentially defunct.

US LED lighting technology company that designs LED chips and arrays used in commercial, industrial and street lighting, and that also supplies light engines to lighting makers worldwide. Customers are lighting fixture manufacturers and system integrators, and revenue comes from selling LED components and licensing its patents. Founded in 2002 and based in Silicon Valley, it was taken over by a Chinese-led investor group in the 2010s. B2B component supplier with low consumer awareness, though its LEDs sit inside many lighting products.

Chinese environmental services group specialising in waste-to-energy, the largest operator of this type in China, building and running incineration power plants, along with biomass, hazardous waste, wind and photovoltaic power, and water treatment. Customers are city governments that pay waste treatment fees, and it also sells electricity to the grid. It is listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange and is controlled by China Everbright Group, a state-owned financial group. B2B infrastructure operator with little consumer visibility, though the Everbright group name is well known in China.

Indian eye care hospital group, one of the largest in the country, running many hospitals and clinics under the Dr. Agarwal's Eye Hospital brand across India, as well as in Africa, treating cataract, retina, cornea, glaucoma and refractive surgery. Customers are patients paying out of pocket or through insurance, and it earns revenue from surgeries and consultations. It is based in Chennai, was founded in 1957 and carries several hundred facilities. A listing on the Indian stock exchanges followed in 2025. Strong healthcare brand in India through TV and digital advertising.

Swedish manufacturer of rolled aluminium products, mainly brazing sheet and strip used in aluminium heat exchangers such as car radiators, air conditioning and cooling systems. Customers are automotive suppliers and heating and cooling manufacturers around the world, with factories in Sweden, China, the US and elsewhere, and revenue comes from supplying high-spec aluminium strip. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm since the mid-2000s, with annual sales of a few billion Swedish kronor. B2B industrial supplier with low consumer visibility.

Malaysian-headquartered streaming service that launched in 2015 to deliver subscription and free video on demand to emerging markets in Southeast Asia, offering local TV, Hollywood films and original content through partnerships. Revenue came from subscriptions, telecom bundles and ads, with millions of users across Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam. The business faced heavy losses and collapsed in 2020, when its assets were bought by Tencent Video. Once a known consumer brand in the region, but no longer operating independently.

US natural gas producer, based in Denver, with its operations focused on the Marcellus Shale in northeastern Pennsylvania, where it drilled wells and sold gas to pipelines and marketers. The company was funded by private equity and venture investors and had small production compared with larger shale operators. Its ownership and current status after later transactions are not well known to me. B2B energy producer with no consumer brand.

Calgary-based energy management company in the oil and gas sector, as described by Crunchbase. The data does not show its assets, production, ownership or operating history, and there are similarly named companies in the Canadian oil industry. It likely owns or manages oil and gas properties in Western Canada. B2B resource business with minimal consumer profile. Details should be verified before outreach. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Irish-registered mining company that operates the Moma titanium minerals mine in northern Mozambique, one of the world's largest producers of ilmenite, and also zircon and rutile, which feed pigment, ceramics and welding industries. Customers are chemical and pigment manufacturers, mostly in China and elsewhere in Asia. The company is dual-listed on the London Stock Exchange and Euronext Dublin. Output is around one million tonnes of ilmenite a year. B2B commodity miner with no consumer brand.

Australian bank and the main banking subsidiary of Macquarie Group, offering personal banking, home loans, business banking, wealth management and asset financing, with the Macquarie brand known for investment banking, infrastructure and commodities trading. Customers include retail clients, businesses and institutions in Australia and globally. Macquarie Group has tens of thousands of employees and operations in more than 30 markets. The Group is listed on the ASX. Strong brand in finance and well known to Australian consumers, with sponsorships in arts and sport.

North Carolina lithium developer that planned to mine and process spodumene from deposits in Gaston County (the Carolina lithium project) and also held an interest in Ewoyaa in Ghana. It sought to supply lithium chemicals to US battery and EV makers, with a lithium offtake agreement with Tesla. In 2025 it merged with Australia's Sayona Mining to form Elevra Lithium. B2B resource developer with no consumer brand awareness.

US digital mortgage lender, based in Pasadena, that offered an online application platform for home loans to borrowers with strong credit, with a model of full-service digital origination and loan officers on call. Revenue comes from origination fees and sale of loans to investors. It raised several hundred million dollars from investors in the 2010s but faced the mortgage market downturn. Consumer-facing but a small brand with little awareness.

Danish online investment bank and trading specialist, known for its SaxoTraderGO platform that lets retail and professional clients trade stocks, forex, futures, bonds and options across tens of thousands of instruments, and for white-label services to banks. Founded in 1992 in Copenhagen, it is majority owned by Geely Holding (since 2018) and has a stake held by Sampo. It has offices in Europe, Asia and the Middle East. It has sponsored sport, including the Saxo-Tinkoff cycling team. Good recognition among active traders and cyclists.

Oklahoma City-based energy company engaged in oil and gas exploration and production, as described by Crunchbase. The data does not provide its fields, production, ownership or current status, and the name is generic, so the identity cannot be confirmed. Likely a privately backed independent producer with no consumer profile. Details should be verified before outreach. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Seattle-based virtual primary care and AI healthcare company that offered text-based consultations with doctors, backed by machine learning to handle patient intake. Customers were employers, health plans and consumers, and revenue came from subscription and visit fees. It raised close to 300 million dollars, including a large 2021 financing round, and was built around a chat-first experience, but struggled with cash and sold its core business assets to Transcarent in 2024. Modest consumer profile.

Brazilian water and sanitation company that operates drinking water supply and sewage services in Rio de Janeiro state, under concession contracts won in an auction in 2021 for part of the old CEDAE state utility, serving millions of customers in dozens of municipalities. It is controlled by the infrastructure group Aegea Saneamento with investors including Itausa and Brookfield. Revenue comes from water tariffs paid by households and businesses. Because it serves residents of the Rio region, it has strong local brand visibility.

Thai conglomerate founded in 1878 as a trading firm, originally from Germany (Berli Jucker/Grimm family), now active in power generation (B.Grimm Power), real estate, healthcare, trading and pharmaceuticals, with the Siemens partnership historically a major business. Customers range from the Thai state electricity authority to hospitals and consumers. Revenue is in the hundreds of billions of baht. B.Grimm Power is listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand. Well-known name in Thai business, with brands in healthcare and power, but limited consumer sports sponsorship history.

US medical device company (Intrinsic Therapeutics) developing the Barricaid annular closure device, an implant designed to close the hole in a spinal disc after surgery for a herniated disc, reducing the chance of reherniation. Customers are spine surgeons and hospitals, with sales in the US and Europe. The company is venture backed. B2B medical device maker with no consumer brand recognition.

US commercial finance company, formerly a Maryland-based specialty lender that turned into a bank holding company, providing commercial loans to small and middle-market businesses such as healthcare, real estate and tech firms. It became a real estate investment trust and then converted back, listed on the NYSE (CSE), and was acquired by PacWest Bancorp in 2014. B2B lender with low consumer profile and no longer an independent company.

Largest independent ATM operator in the world, deploying and running around 200,000 ATMs in retail stores, convenience stores and bank branches across the US, UK, Canada, Mexico, Germany and Australia, and also providing managed ATM services for banks under the Allpoint and bank-branded networks. Revenue is surcharge and interchange fees from cardholders and banks. Listed on Nasdaq (CATM) and acquired by NCR in 2021 for about 2.5 billion dollars. Consumer-facing machines are ubiquitous, but the company name is little known to the public.

US midstream natural gas company that gathered, processed and transported natural gas and natural gas liquids in Texas, Oklahoma and Louisiana. Customers were producers and utilities. Listed on Nasdaq (CPNO) as a master limited partnership and acquired by Kinder Morgan in 2013 for about 5 billion dollars. B2B energy infrastructure with no consumer brand. Its networks of pipelines and plants were among the larger independent midstream systems in the Texas and Oklahoma gas fields, handling large daily volumes.

US account-based marketing and sales software company providing AI-enabled tools that help business-to-business marketers identify target companies, personalise ads and prioritise outreach. Customers include enterprise technology and manufacturing firms who pay annual software subscriptions, and the product integrates intent data and advertising. Founded in 2006 as a lead gen tool, it grew over time into account-based marketing. Raised capital from investors including Bain Capital, and has hundreds of employees. B2B with well-known brand in marketing technology circles, little consumer awareness.

Austin-based finance and medical business, described in Crunchbase as offering support and growth for healthcare practices, and tagged for financial services. The information is too limited to say which medical practices or investors it serves, or its ownership, and there may be unrelated firms with similar names. Likely a small private B2B business.
